earlier_scan.source_named: Stolz, Michael 1911. Die Umgebung von Kap Koenig Wilhelm (22pp, GlottologGlottolog's fullest description is a phonology or text collection); Suter 2018 Comparative Morphology of the Huon Peninsula Languages read online but contains no Sialum stress statement

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1975. North-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38: 527-567.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress/accent/tone/pitch remarks anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent printed pp.527-567); no Sialum-specific phonology.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1970. The Selepet language within the Finisterre-Huon phylum (New Guinea). PhD thesis, ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stress statements are for Selepet only; Sialum mentioned only historically (Stolz opened the Sialum mission station in 1907).

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Sialum' (lexicon from McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970)
sources.note: Wordlist only (no stress marks); used to confirm Dempwolff's Pon/Keseraua = Sialum.

sources.citation: Suter, Edgar. 2018. Comparative Morphology of the Huon Peninsula Languages (Papua New Guinea). PhD dissertation, Universitaet zu Koeln. viii+331 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Sialum stress. p.6: 'the only publication that survives is an ethnographic report containing a glossed mythological text (Stolz 1911). My main source for Sialum is McElhanon's survey fieldnotes.' Sialum appears only in object-verb/pronoun paradigms.

sources.citation: Phinnemore, Thomas R. 1985. Ono phonology and morphophonemics. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22, Pacific Linguistics A-63: 173-214.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the sister language Ono (stress-group analysis); Sialum named once as a neighbouring language, nothing about Sialum stress.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1973. Towards a typology of the Finisterre-Huon languages, New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-22. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Divinity School Library (offsite storage), call number - Ask at Circulation (Pamph. folio) BS 354 .Z91
sources.note: Sialum only in the language list (Western Huon family, d.); the phonology section (phonemes, syllable structure, morphophonemics) says nothing about stress for any language.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1919. The Languages of Northern Papua. Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 49: 317-341.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classificatory overview; lists 'Kamoka', 'Pong', 'Keseraua', 'Ago' (villages near Cape King William) in the Papuan 'Kai Group' (p.321), evidently from Dempwolff's specimens; no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Stolz, Michael. 1911. Die Umgebung von Kap Koenig Wilhelm. In Richard Neuhauss (ed.), Deutsch Neu-Guinea, Band III: Beitraege der Missionare Keysser, Stolz, Zahn, Lehner, Bamler, 244-286. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for Sialum (ethnographic report with a glossed Sialum myth text by the missionary who worked at Sialum from 1907); the only place a remark on Sialum pronunciation/Betonung or accent-marked text could exist in print. Full-view scans exist but were could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Dempwolff, Otto. 1905. Beitraege zur Kenntnis der Sprachen von Deutsch-Neuguinea. Mitteilungen des Seminars fuer Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin VIII, Abt. 1: 182-254. Section II 'Papuasprachen' b) Pon '(Dorf bei Kap Koenig Wilhelm)' p.243, c) Keseraua '(Dorf etwa 5 km von Pon)' pp.243-244, d) Ago '(Dorf bei Festungshuk, suedlich Kap Koenig Wilhelm)' p.245; transcription conventions p.182.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No rule for this language. p.182 gives only his marking convention ('Die Betonung pflegte ich oft nicht zu bezeichnen, wenn sie der uns gelaeufigen auf der vorletzten Silbe entsprach'). The Pon and Keseraua wordlists (Kap Koenig Wilhelm = Sialum; forms match McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970 Sialum: na 'I', yana 'he', denan 'eye', wauwa 'dog', nani 'bird', namu 'breast') carry acute stress marks on many items (ka'sa, ka'mu, we'sap, la'lam, go-so'n, ka'te, u'nu, be'ra, pe'sum, na'ni, ya'ra, sa-xo'-rup, kon-do'-ro, ta'mba; ma'ma, ne-sa'd-na, be-le-ka'm-na, di'-na-na, sa-ga-ra'-na, ke-na'm-na, me-ta'-n…

sources.citation: Phinnemore, Thomas R. & Penny Phinnemore. n.d. Ono grammar sketch / Ono grammar essentials (unpublished SIL-PNG ms., cited by Suter 2018).

sources.note: Sister language of Sialum within the Kalasa subfamily; only in-depth description in the subfamily (Phinnemore 1985 Ono phonology is already held) -- useful only as a sibling proxy, not for Sialum itself.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1967. Preliminary Observations on Huon Peninsula Languages. Oceanic Linguistics 6(1): 1-45.

sources.note: Earliest phonological survey of Huon Peninsula languages with general remarks on Huon phonologies; TransNewGuinea.org indicates Sialum is not among the 14 languages with data, but the general phonology remarks (and any family-level stress statement) should be checked.

sources.citation: McElhanon, Kenneth A. [1966-67]. Sialum survey fieldnotes (wordlists and verb paradigms), unpublished; held by SIL-PNG / used by Suter 2018; audio in PARADISEC collection KM1.

sources.note: Suter 2018's 'main source for Sialum'; the only modern linguist's transcription of Sialum, may carry stress marks or notes.
